response.title: Is it better to buy two 100 watt folding solar panels or one 200 watt panel for a power station?
response.answer:
For most portable power stations, I'd recommend two 100W folding solar panels over one 200W folding panel, assuming similar quality, efficiency, and price.

However, if you prioritize simplicity and quick setup, one 200W panel may be better.

Why I'd lean toward two 100W panels

You can position each panel independently to maximize sunlight, especially when camping around trees or uneven terrain.

Shop

One 200W panel

Fewer connections, potentially less wiring loss, and usually faster setup. Better when you have an unobstructed sunny location.

The most important consideration: electrical compatibility

Two 100W panels can be connected in two ways:

Parallel: Voltage stays the same, current adds together. Often suitable for power stations with lower solar input voltage limits.

Series: Voltage adds together, current stays the same. Can reduce cable losses, but the combined open-circuit voltage must remain below your power station's maximum input voltage, including in cold weather.

Also, two panels don't necessarily charge faster than one. If your power station accepts only 100W of solar input, neither 200W configuration will deliver its full rated power.

My recommendation

Camping, RV trips, or changing sunlight: Two 100W panels.

Backyard charging or simple emergency backup: One 200W panel.

Best value: Whichever offers the better price per watt, compatible electrical specifications, and better build quality.

One important question: What brand and model is your power station? (EcoFlow, Jackery, Bluetti, Anker, etc.)

With that information, I can tell you which configuration is better for its actual charging performance, including whether series or parallel wiring makes more sense.
